supports: The US Census Bureau provides a computer- and internet-use data series covering 1984 through 2009.
does_not_support: It does not show that household computer use caused a particular workplace or labour-market change.

supports: BLS reports an 80.4% decline in US employment of word processors and typists from 1999 to 2018 and states that offshoring complicates attribution of occupational change to automation or AI.
does_not_support: It does not isolate office software as the sole cause, nor does it establish effects for all clerical work.

supports: Using representative US task-requirement data from 1960–98, the study associates computerization with lower relative demand for routine cognitive and manual tasks and higher relative demand for non-routine cognitive tasks.
does_not_support: It does not show that every computerised workplace upgraded work or that a worker can reliably protect their position through individual skill acquisition.

supports: For US office and administrative support jobs in the study's 2007 and 2010–16 postings data, software adoption at job-title level was associated with higher applicant skill requirements and broader task content; local gains primarily accrued to college-educated women.
does_not_support: It does not establish a causal outcome for all office workers, all countries, or today's AI tools.
affected_people: US office and administrative support applicants

supports: The paper presents ATMs as a case in which automation of cash-dispensing tasks coincided with banks operating more branches and tellers moving toward customer-service work, offsetting the simple per-branch substitution story.
does_not_support: It does not show that ATMs had no distributional effects or that future automation will create offsetting demand.

supports: For US commuting zones exposed to industrial robots from 1990–2007, the study estimates lower employment-to-population ratios and wages as robot exposure increased.
does_not_support: It does not show that robots caused the same effect in every workplace, or that the estimate transfers to office software or AI.
affected_people: workers in robot-exposed US commuting zones

supports: A retrospective IMF article offers ATM and accounting-software examples as prompts to inspect task and organisational change.
does_not_support: It does not establish prevalence, causal effects, or a general employment outcome.
affected_people: workers discussed in retrospective automation narratives
